item.title: A look at the largest clergy abuse settlements reached by Catholic organizations in the US
item.description: Here is a list of some of the other large clergy abuse settlements reached by the Catholic Church in the United States.

item.title: Polish bishop on trial over alleged delays in reporting claims of child abuse by priests
item.description: A Polish bishop went on trial Wednesday, accused of not informing authorities immediately about alleged sexual abuse of children by two priests in his diocese.

item.title: Artificial Intelligence is growing fast, making the Church face new challenges
item.description: Pope Leo XIV seems to know the issue of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is more than a barroom debate, as the new technology continues to grow at an exponential rate.

item.title: The travertine quarries that built St. Peter’s Square are carving rock for Mormon temple
item.description: Today, the same quarries that built Rome with their distinctive travertine are still being dug out to build a new generation of churches, temples and mosques around the world — as well as banks, museums, government buildings and private homes.

item.title: Catholics return to confession focused on grace, not a get-out-of-hell-free card
item.description: The Lenten period for penance started this week with Ash Wednesday, and some Catholic priests are happily bracing for long lines outside the confessional. The faithful across the United States are embracing anew the sacrament.

item.title: Pope’s grand tour of Italy over the next few months takes him to Lampedusa and beyond
item.description: Pope Leo XIV will visit ground zero of Europe’s migration drama, the Sicilian island of Lampedusa, in May and also minister to Italians poisoned by years of toxic dumping by the mafia, according to travel plans announced on Thursday by the Vatican.

item.title: Breakaway Catholic group rejects Vatican talks, indicating collision course for pope
item.description: A breakaway Catholic traditionalist group on Thursday rejected the Vatican’s offer of talks, suggesting a collision course with Pope Leo XIV over its planned consecrations of new bishops without his consent.

item.title: Crux Exclusive: Card. Ambongo on historic AU partnership for ‘The Africa We Want’
item.description: In an exclusive interview with Crux, Card. Fridolin Ambongo says the new agreement is a favorable and decisive moment for the continent.

item.title: Kosovo’s Catholics and Muslims mark Ash Wednesday and Ramadan in one week
item.description: Kosovo ‘s religious diversity came to light this week as the Balkan nation’s Christian and Muslim communities both embarked on a traditional period of fasting and spiritual reflection.

item.title: Full canonical penal process may be opened against Spanish bishop accused of sexual abuse
item.description: A preliminary investigation by the Roman Rota into the allegations against a Spanish bishop accused of sexual abuse of a minor has recommended that the Vatican open a full canonical penal process.
